introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Statistics Paper 2 (0770/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

Le sujet n'imprime aucun total par question ni pour l'épreuve ; les points imprimés par bloc ((i), (ii)...) sont recopiés tels quels (leur somme est 103). Quand un même total couvre plusieurs sous-questions (ex. « (9 marks) » pour (a) et (b)), il est porté par la dernière sous-question du bloc, les autres ont `points` null, et `points` de chaque exercice est laissé vide.

Scan de 3 pages (page de garde + 2 pages de questions) : les questions 1 à 10 sont complètes et se suivent, aucune page ne semble manquer. L'étiquette en haut à gauche de la page de garde dit « Pure Maths With Stats 2 », en accord avec le cadre (Pure Mathematics With Statistics, Paper 2, code 0770) et le pied de page 00/0770/2.

questions.enonce_markdown: When the polynomial $P(x)$, where $P(x) = 2x^3 + ax^2 + bx - 12$, is divided by $(x + 3)$ the remainder is $18$. Given that $(x + 1)$ is a factor of $P(x)$, find the values of the constants $a$ and $b$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Remainder theorem.** The remainder on division by $(x + 3)$ is $P(-3)$, so $P(-3) = 18$:
$$2(-3)^3 + a(-3)^2 + b(-3) - 12 = 18 \;\Rightarrow\; -54 + 9a - 3b - 12 = 18 \;\Rightarrow\; 9a - 3b = 84 \;\Rightarrow\; 3a - b = 28. \qquad (1)$$

**Factor theorem.** $(x + 1)$ is a factor, so $P(-1) = 0$:
$$2(-1)^3 + a(-1)^2 + b(-1) - 12 = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; -2 + a - b - 12 = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; a - b = 14. \qquad (2)$$

**Solve.** Subtract (2) from (1): $2a = 14$, so $a = 7$. Then from (2), $b = a - 14 = -7$.

Check: $P(x) = 2x^3 + 7x^2 - 7x - 12$ gives $P(-3) = -54 + 63 + 21 - 12 = 18$ and $P(-1) = -2 + 7 + 7 - 12 = 0$.
$$\boxed{a = 7, \quad b = -7}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: With the values of $a$ and $b$ found in part (i)(a), factorise $P(x) = 2x^3 + ax^2 + bx - 12$ completely. (9 marks for part (i), (a) and (b) together)
questions.corrige_markdown:
From part (i)(a), $P(x) = 2x^3 + 7x^2 - 7x - 12$, and $(x + 1)$ is a factor. Divide by $(x + 1)$ (long division or comparing coefficients): $P(x) = (x + 1)(2x^2 + cx - 12)$. Expanding, the coefficient of $x^2$ is $c + 2 = 7$, so $c = 5$; the coefficient of $x$ is $-12 + c = -7$, which agrees.
$$P(x) = (x + 1)(2x^2 + 5x - 12).$$
Factorise the quadratic: we need two numbers with product $2 \times (-12) = -24$ and sum $5$, namely $8$ and $-3$:
$$2x^2 + 5x - 12 = 2x^2 + 8x - 3x - 12 = 2x(x + 4) - 3(x + 4) = (2x - 3)(x + 4).$$
$$\boxed{P(x) = (x + 1)(2x - 3)(x + 4)}$$
The zeros are $x = -4$, $x = -1$ and $x = \tfrac32$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the range of values of $k \in \mathbb{R}$, for which the roots of the quadratic equation $x^2 + kx + 3 + k = 0$ are real and distinct. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $x^2 + kx + (3 + k) = 0$ we have $a = 1$, $b = k$, $c = 3 + k$. The roots are real and distinct if and only if the discriminant is strictly positive:
$$\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = k^2 - 4(3 + k) = k^2 - 4k - 12 > 0.$$
Factorise: $k^2 - 4k - 12 = (k - 6)(k + 2)$. The parabola $\Delta(k) = (k - 6)(k + 2)$ opens upward and is zero at $k = -2$ and $k = 6$, so it is positive outside the interval between the zeros:
$$(k - 6)(k + 2) > 0 \iff k < -2 \ \text{ or } \ k > 6.$$
Check: $k = 7$ gives $x^2 + 7x + 10 = (x+2)(x+5)$, two distinct real roots; $k = 0$ gives $x^2 + 3 = 0$, no real root.
$$\boxed{k < -2 \ \text{ or } \ k > 6}$$
